record.narrative:
I used the signed convention already in force: for direction -1, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a weaker, less negative dependency score. Clinical importance was judged against a roughly 10%-of-absolute-mean scale for each outcome: SMARCA2 approximately 0.0415, WRN approximately 0.0301, NFE2L2 approximately 0.0093, USP7 approximately 0.0093, DHX9 approximately 0.0249, MDM2 approximately 0.0269, BRAF approximately 0.0248, EGFR approximately 0.025, and KRAS approximately 0.0245. These are supplied-dataset discovery associations, not causal or externally generalizable claims.

The high-Cas9 adenocarcinoma context tests for the four accepted large signals were uniformly strong. H127, SMARCA2 dependency in SMARCA4-loss adenocarcinoma screens with Cas9 activity at least 0.846, gave R91 = +0.7852, interval +0.7575 to +0.8129. H128, WRN dependency in MSI-high adenocarcinoma high-Cas9 screens, gave R92 = +0.7831, interval +0.7404 to +0.8257. H129, weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss adenocarcinoma high-Cas9 screens, gave R93 = +0.7859, interval +0.7559 to +0.8158. H130, weaker USP7 dependency in TP53-loss adenocarcinoma high-Cas9 screens, gave R94 = +0.8136, interval +0.7840 to +0.8431. For each outcome, the lower bound is many times the relevant clinical scale, so the exact high-quality subtype contexts are clinically supported with very favorable uncertainty. I accepted and closed these exact context claims because their scientific question, whether the headline signals persist under both adenocarcinoma and high-Cas9 screening restrictions, is now resolved in the affirmative. This strengthens the internal coherence of the accepted large associations but does not imply causality or generalizability beyond the dataset.

The ARID1A co-loss context produced a nuanced but consistent result. H132 tests SMARCA4 loss in lines that also have ARID1A loss: R96 = +0.8143, interval +0.7666 to +0.8620. This is again far above the SMARCA2 clinical threshold, so the SMARCA4-loss associated stronger SMARCA2 dependency remains extremely large when ARID1A is also lost. I accepted and closed H132. By contrast, H21 tests whether the SMARCA4-loss effect formally differs by ARID1A status: R95 = +0.0373, interval -0.0148 to +0.0894. The point estimate is modest relative to SMARCA2 clinical scale, and the interval crosses null while also reaching above threshold. This neither establishes an important positive interaction nor cleanly excludes a moderate interaction. H21 remains unresolved and deferred; H132 is more scientifically informative as an exact context effect, whereas the interaction remains imprecise.

The specificity and secondary-pathway controls mostly produced clinically meaningful nulls or opposite effects. H135 tests whether SMARCA4 loss also produces stronger DHX9 dependency. R97 = -0.0055, interval -0.0249 to +0.0138. For direction -1, the clinically meaningful claim requires positive effects above about +0.0249; the upper bound is below that, so the DHX9 specificity control rejects a clinically meaningful stronger DHX9 effect. This supports the outcome specificity of the large SMARCA4/SMARCA2 association. H136 tests whether TP53 loss is associated with stronger WRN dependency. R98 = -0.0054, interval -0.0342 to +0.0235. The upper bound is below the WRN clinical scale of about +0.0301, so the registered stronger-WRN TP53-loss claim is rejected. H142 tests whether KRAS mutation is associated with weaker BRAF dependency, R100 = -0.0164, interval -0.0343 to +0.0014. The interval is centered on the opposite of the weaker-BRAF hypothesis and the upper bound is far below the BRAF clinical scale, so the claim is rejected. H111 tests whether PTEN loss is associated with stronger EGFR dependency among KRAS-mutant high-Cas9 screens. R101 = -0.0351, interval -0.0812 to +0.0111. The positive upper bound is below the EGFR clinical scale, and the point estimate is in the opposite direction, so the registered stronger-EGFR claim is rejected. This helps the already downgraded PTEN-loss EGFR program: the signal does not appear to extend into KRAS-mutant high-Cas9 cells, although the PTEN program as a whole is not currently supported.

Two smaller programs remain scientifically possible but not established. H138 refines the MDM2 TP53-loss test in high-Cas9 screens: R99 = +0.0226, interval -0.0099 to +0.0552. For direction +1, this means weaker MDM2 dependency with TP53 loss, which is biologically plausible through the canonical p53-MDM2 axis. The point estimate is below the MDM2 clinical scale of about +0.0269, but the upper bound exceeds it. The exact claim is unresolved and deferred rather than rejected because the interval does not exclude a clinically meaningful effect. H23 tests KRAS mutation versus wild-type KRAS dependency in adenocarcinoma: R102 = +0.0115, interval -0.0094 to +0.0324. The point is below the KRAS clinical scale but the upper bound exceeds it, so the exact claim remains unresolved and active. It is a low-confidence candidate, and the pending high-Cas9 adenocarcinoma refinement H139 is more informative than pursuing this broad claim further now.

For validation, I request H9, the original MSI-high versus MSI-non-high WRN dependency claim. It has one of the four headline large effects, R9 = +0.7899, but unlike several other headline claims it has not been independently validated. The new H128 result strengthens its coherence in a clean high-Cas9 adenocarcinoma context, so independent validation of the core MSI-high WRN association is now useful. If validation is favorable, the WRN MSI-high association becomes much more robust; if validation is unfavorable, WRN/MSI-high should be downgraded alongside the accepted large-signal set. No further validation is requested for PTEN or EGFR at this point because the exact best-selected PTEN EGFR context already failed independent validation.

Iteration 8/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

Third, H135 is a non-target specificity control: if SMARCA4 loss is specifically associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, it should not show a comparably large clinically meaningful shift in DHX9 dependency. H136 and H138 probe additional TP53-loss biology on outcomes not yet strongly linked to TP53 loss. record.narrative: Signed convention used throughout: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a weaker, less negative dependency score. Clinical significance was assessed against a roughly 10 percent relative-difference scale for each outcome; for these dependency scores this corresponds to absolute effects on the order of 0.009 to 0.042, whereas the accepted large dependency programs have estimates near 0.78 to 0.82, many multiples above threshold. All claims below are dataset-specific association statements, not causal or externally generalizable claims. H9, MSI-high versus MSI-non-high WRN dependency direction -1, received validation R103: signed +0.8218 with adjusted interval +0.7685 to +0.8752 in cells of 105 exposed and 1895 comparator, alongside discovery R9 of +0.7899. The validation interval excludes null and has a lower bound more than twenty-fold above the approximate WRN clinical scale of about 0.030. This strongly supports the core supplied-dataset association that MSI-high lines show much stronger WRN dependency. I therefore accept and close H9 as the exact comparison resolved by independent validation. H10, MYC amplification versus no MYC amplification for DHX9 dependency direction -1, is now decisively unsupported: discovery R10 was negative and clinically null, and validation R77 was signed -0.0264 with adjusted interval -0.0595 to +0.0066, again opposite to the claimed stronger-DHX9-dependency direction and not supporting a clinically meaningful positive effect. I reject and close H10. H95, NF1 loss versus NF1 wild type among KRAS and BRAF wild type cells for KRAS dependency direction +1, had a favorable discovery signal R65 but failed independent validation: R76 was signed -0.0161 with adjusted interval -0.0621 to +0.0299, crossing null and pointing the opposite direction from the claimed weaker KRAS dependency. The exact selected context therefore does not replicate, so I reject and close H95. This downgrades the NF1 bypass-to-KRAS-dependency program; broader NF1 claims remain unresolved and low priority rather than supported. H106, TP53 loss versus TP53 wild type among adenocarcinoma KRAS wild type cells for MDM2 dependency direction +1, is also rejected: discovery R75 was near null, and validation R104 was signed -0.0301 with adjusted interval -0.0808 to +0.0206, crossing null and opposite to the claimed weaker MDM2 dependency. This exact MDM2 TP53-loss context fails independent validation, so the canonical TP53-loss weaker-MDM2-dependency candidate is not supported here and is deprioritized. Overall, the supported evidence continues to be dominated by four large supplied-dataset dependency programs: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency; MSI-high is associated with much stronger WRN dependency; KEAP1 loss is associated with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, after the original opposite-direction claim was rejected; and TP53 loss is associated with much weaker USP7 dependency. Several of these have independent validation, including WRN and USP7 now, and many context analyses show large effects across co-mutational, batch, screening-quality, and subtype subsets. The main negative findings now include failed validation for MYC-DHX9, NF1-loss KRAS dependency, PTEN-loss EGFR dependency in the best selected high-Cas9 KRAS wild type adenocarcinoma context, and TP53-loss MDM2 dependency in the adenocarcinoma KRAS wild type context, plus specificity nulls for POLR2A broad shifts and several non-target controls. Remaining uncertainty is concentrated in weaker candidate programs, including EGFR-amplification and KRAS-mutation associations, KIF18A TP53-loss signals, POLR2A specificity controls, ARID1A interaction precision, marker negative controls, and the high-Cas9 MDM2 refinement. The most informative next analyses are to test whether the four headline large dependency associations remain very large specifically in high Cas9 activity and Avana-library screens; persistence would reduce concern that screening-library or Cas9-quality confounding drives the headline signals, whereas attenuation would identify an important technical context boundary.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

The new proposals are discovery associations within the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims. The first set tests accepted large signals. dependency_SMARCA2 and smarca4_loss in ARID1A-loss lines asks whether the synthetic-lethal SMARCA2 signal remains extremely large when ARID1A is also lost. If ARID1A co-loss strongly attenuates or reverses it, that would indicate important context dependence; if it remains large, it strengthens the supplied-dataset association. dependency_POLR2A in high-Cas9 screens for SMARCA4 loss and KEAP1 loss is a core-transcription specificity control. A clinically meaningful positive signed effect on POLR2A would suggest those predictors may capture broad transcriptional, proliferative, or screening effects rather than outcome-specific biology; near-null or opposite effects support specificity. dependency_DHX9 and smarca4_loss adds another non-target specificity check. The second set focuses on TP53 loss. dependency_WRN and tp53_loss tests whether p53-deficient cells become more dependent on WRN, perhaps because WRN helps resolve replication stress or stalled forks when p53 checkpoint control is lost. The plausible alternatives are no association or weaker dependency due to altered stress signaling. dependency_RPL11 and tp53_loss tests the classical ribosome-p53-MDM2 axis: RPL11 can help restrain MDM2 and activate p53, so p53 loss may weaken the need for RPL11, hence direction +1. dependency_MDM2 and tp53_loss refines the near-null overall MDM2 TP53-loss test by restricting to higher Cas9 activity, where technical noise is lower. A clinically meaningful weaker MDM2 dependency in TP53-loss lines is biologically plausible because MDM2's main target is p53; a persistent null would make MDM2 less compelling. The third set resolves smaller RTK and MAPK signals. dependency_KRAS and kras_mutation in adenocarcinoma high-Cas9 tests whether the weak overall KRAS-mutation association becomes meaningful in the subtype where KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinoma is common and screening quality is better. If it remains near null, the KRAS-mutation association is not clinically supported despite biological plausibility. dependency_EGFR and egfr_amplification excluding ERBB2 co-amplification in high-Cas9 tests whether the borderline EGFR-amplification signal is diluted by co-amplified ERBB2 lines or low-quality screens. Similarly, dependency_ERBB2 and erbb2_amplification excluding EGFR co-amplification in high-Cas9 tests a cleaner ERBB2-amplification hypothesis. If these remain subthreshold, I will treat the RTK programs as unresolved but deprioritized. dependency_BRAF and kras_mutation tests MAPK pathway crosstalk: KRAS-mutant cells bypass BRAF, so a plausible hypothesis is weaker BRAF dependency, hence direction +1. If it remains below the clinical scale, the KIF18A TP53-loss program should be closed or deferred rather than further expanded. Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation

record.narrative: Signed convention remains: for direction -1, a positive signed estimate means exposed cells have a stronger, more negative dependency score; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means exposed cells have a weaker, less negative dependency score. Using approximate 10-percent clinical scales, accepted large programs are many multiples above threshold. H7 receives independent validation: R117 is +0.792 with adjusted lower bound +0.765, confirming discovery R7 +0.784; the effect is about 18 times the SMARCA2 clinical scale of about 0.0415, so I accept and close the exact SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency claim. This completes independent validation for the four headline programs: SMARCA4 loss stronger SMARCA2, MSI-high stronger WRN, KEAP1 loss weaker NFE2L2, and TP53 loss weaker USP7. H105 response deadline is resolved by R90: validation is +0.0148 with interval -0.0444 to +0.0740, crossing null and with a point estimate below the EGFR clinical scale of about 0.025, despite discovery R74 +0.0435. I reject and close this exact selected PTEN-loss EGFR context; it does not support accepting a clinically meaningful EGFR-amplification or PTEN-loss EGFR claim. The broader H96 PTEN-loss EGFR context remains unresolved but deprioritized because the best selected high-quality context failed. Supported findings are therefore limited to the four large dataset-specific associations plus many accepted context refinements; these are not causal or external claims. Negative or unsupported programs include MYC-DHX9, NF1-loss KRAS selected context, TP53-loss MDM2 adenocarcinoma KRAS wild-type context, PTEN-loss EGFR high-quality selected context, broad POLR2A TP53-loss weaker control, and marker negative controls. Unresolved uncertainty remains around modest KRAS-mutation and EGFR-amplification effects, KIF18A TP53-loss direction with clinical threshold uncertainty, broad PTEN-loss EGFR, POLR2A specificity controls, and small co-context interactions. The most informative next analyses are pre-registered high-quality Avana/high-Cas9 tests for KIF18A TP53-loss, EGFR amplification in KRAS wild-type adenocarcinoma, KRAS mutation in adenocarcinoma, and library/Cas9 boundary checks for SMARCA2, NFE2L2, and USP7, plus a lower-priority MDM2 high-quality test. Future acceptance should require robust discovery intervals excluding the relevant 10-percent threshold and, when feasible, independent validation; selected post hoc contexts should be treated as exploratory.

record.narrative: No assessments are due. The four accepted dataset-specific dependency programs remain internally validated: SMARCA4 loss associated with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high associated with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and TP53 loss associated with weaker USP7 dependency. These remain associations in the supplied dataset, not causal or externally generalizable claims. Signed convention remains: for direction -1, a positive returned estimate means the exposed group has a stronger, more negative dependency score; for direction +1, a positive returned estimate means the exposed group has a weaker, less negative dependency score. Approximate 10-percent clinical scales remain about 0.042 for SMARCA2, 0.030 for WRN, 0.009 for NFE2L2, 0.009 for USP7, and 0.025 to 0.026 for KIF18A, POLR2A, and RPL11. The first two proposals are focused boundary tests. KIF18A TP53-loss dependency in high-Cas9 Avana adenocarcinoma screens refines the near-threshold KIF18A signal: a robust positive signed effect above about 0.025 would support TP53 loss associated with stronger KIF18A dependency in a high-quality adenocarcinoma context, while an interval crossing zero or remaining near threshold would keep this claim unresolved. SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 dependency under low Cas9 activity tests whether the very large SMARCA2 program persists when screening quality is lower; persistence would reduce concern that it is restricted to high-Cas9 contexts, while attenuation would identify technical context dependence. The next four proposals are pre-specified phenotype-state interaction tests within high-quality Avana contexts. SMARCA2 is tested in high versus low EMT state, WRN in high versus low EMT state, NFE2L2 in high versus low hypoxia state, and USP7 in high versus low stemness state. The main hypotheses are that EMT-high state strengthens the SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 effect, hypoxia-high state amplifies KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and stemness-high state amplifies TP53-loss weaker USP7 dependency; WRN is registered with uncertain state modification because the MSI-high effect could be either chromatin-remodeling-specific or broadly proliferation-associated. A positive signed interaction in the accepted program direction means the effect is larger in the high-state subgroup than in its complement; a near-null interaction favors context stability. The remaining six proposals are cross-predictor and broad-essentiality specificity controls in high-Cas9 Avana screens. KEAP1 loss versus USP7 and TP53 loss versus NFE2L2 test whether the accepted oxidative-stress and p53-associated effects cross into the other stress dependency program. SMARCA4 loss versus WRN and MSI-high versus SMARCA2 test whether the large SMARCA2 and WRN programs spill over to non-matched outcomes. TP53 loss versus RPL11 and SMARCA4 loss versus POLR2A test whether accepted predictors also shift broadly essential transcription or ribosomal dependency programs. Clinically large non-matched or essentiality effects would weaken narrow interpretation of the accepted programs; near-null or below-threshold intervals would support outcome specificity, although wide intervals should remain unresolved rather than be accepted as definitive specificity proof. No validation is requested during exploration; validation should be considered at appraisal only if a new focused follow-up is robust and clinically sized.
